paragraphs.text:
A gruff voice snaps, “Drop guns!” You hear the click of rifle 
levers  and  look  up  to  see  several  hunters  on  either  side  of 
you, with weapons leveled. Resistance would be exceptionally 
foolish. You instruct the students to disarm and take a look at 
your captors.

You recognize indicators of the Tsuut’ina, apparently a very 
isolated group, since their old-fashioned skin shirts, leggings, 
and woodland-style moccasins indicate minimal contact with 
the outside. Their rifles are from the 19th century; some are 
single-shot. Charlie said something about outcasts—could this 
be the group she mentioned?

You keep your voice even and address the man who spoke. 
“We mean no harm.”

“Be silent!” the leader grunts and nudges you with a rifle barrel. 
Taking the hint, you follow your captors to a secluded spot.
